touches.text: The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien. Akien, 2026-11-11, Q#85: "you and me. later there will be a specific agent for it, but that's so far off we're not even thinking about it now except 'after the outline is implemented'." So until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both of us read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.

Test tiers. Akien 2026-11-13, from Silicon Spice around 2000: commit, hourly, daily and weekly tests. The complete compiler test ran 40 hours across two executors, so it ran weekly, and the tiers below it meant commit time needed only smoke tests.

Hourly: an entry on Cairn's scheduled list (5.9) reseals every yellow component and everything that depends on it. Commit a is fine and commit b is fine, and an hour later the run finds a new red. That is the system doing what it was designed to do (Akien 2026-11-13), and the window to search is one hour's landings. Hourly confirmed by Akien 2026-11-13: "perfect. yes that."

Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Akien 2026-11-13: "every test failure, every orphaned file, HAS TO BE FIXED. if we get 3 reds but they're really not related to what we just did, we can ticket them for fixing. reds don't get lost." and "so each run writes any new bugs". Once a red unrelated to a crossing is ticketed, that crossing can go ahead.
VERBS: run, notices, CodeMother's verbs reached over the bus (RULE 1). COMMANDS: cairn codemother test (--hollow, --seal, --exec, ...), shortcut cairn test; proofgate (the hook: proofs run by hand).
The chart chain machines (9.3.2): orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict.
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
